title: The Help: the Ref button paragraph into sub-bullets
⌃⌘G doesn't cycle on a retyped number
Helium bookmarks: "the bar did not show" once in a whole run
detail: Asked: found while playing S6's Helium verdict at 17:28: the bookmarks section failed with 'the bar did not show' (selected 0) at 'fb over a selection'; alone it passed 3 of 3. Why: a step that fails once in a whole run blocks an approve and costs a replay. Done when: the step holds its selection's race and the whole run passes it, measured over several runs. Paused (18:34): not reproduced in 12 whole runs since 8874ab6, nor alone (3), slowed 4x and 8x (4), or with its module's sections (3); a ProseMirror focus race was probed and ruled out (30 of 30 kept). 8874ab6 makes the next failure print the page's last selection calls with their callers. Reactivates when: 'the bar did not show' appears in any Helium run: read its calls to find what emptied the selection.

title: Taliessin through Logres: no page labels, the last page's notes as ::: note fences on their poems
detail: Asked: review the formatting of Williams, or perhaps older works in general (22:17): "The fact that the two Williams pieces I looked at have this problem suggest that it's a wider problem." Begun as S13 on Taliessin through Logres: "none of the pages have both prose and verse, so there it should probably just be 'Line ____', and the notes on the final page should probably be turned into ::: note fences on the poems they refer to. And we probably don't need page numbers at all." Also: "all the italic lines in the poems in Taliessin through Logres are part of the poem and should have line numbers (so <line>)." Victorian Narrative Verse "has hard-coded line numbers at the ends of lines, and footnotes to verse before the ::: note block existed so probably needs to be reformatted" (not read all the way through). Why: page labels give 44 Williams entries a Line-or-Page bar (MEASURED), notes sit apart from what they gloss, italic lines of the poems go unnumbered, and typed line numbers stand in the text; two works read, both with these, so likely more. Done when: the older works' formatting is surveyed (which works, which faults, counted over the backup), each fault has a decided form, and one-offs' import folders set them right, each review page read before import.

title: begin refused its own carried items
detail: Asked: `node tools/progress/log.ts begin` answered "the day has not begun: run begin first" (07:20). Why: the batch's carries were read against the day's file alone, before their own begin was written; any day with items carried in could not begin. Done when: a begin batch is read against the day as it will stand, test-first, and the day begun.

title: A terminal copy in two pre blocks pasted as a paragraph per coloured run
detail: Asked: "which feels like a regression. It used to be much more connected, we did a fix for that within the last week." Why: cmux's Ghostty gave one copy as two white-space: pre blocks; terminalCopy took only one, so the copy fell to the editor's HTML paste. Done when: a copy of two blocks or more pastes as its text, test-first, the reader's own copy measured in both views and hand-checked in Helium.

title: A terminal copy's paragraphs keep the terminal's two-space indent
detail: Asked: seen in the hand-check of S14: every paragraph after the first starts with two spaces ("  The cause:"), stored as "\  " after a list. Why: the indent is the terminal's margin, not the text. Done when: a terminal copy's paragraphs paste without the margin, code blocks and nested list items keeping theirs, test-first and played in Helium.

title: A Process list, last, for the tools and the process
detail: Asked: "Maybe a new Chore list or Infrastructure or Process for items like this?" then "yes on the P Process list. It should definitely be at the bottom, so app-specific work goes first." Why: the begin fix and items like it are not app work and had no list. Done when: P is a list, drawn last, test-first.

title: The titles checker missed a test whose assertions changed under its title
detail: Asked: found in S15 (07:58): npm run test:titles said "no test changed under the same description" though the wrapped-lines test in src/editor/paste.test.ts changed two assertions under an unchanged title. Why: the checker is what makes a title be read against changed assertions; a miss lets a stale title through. Done when: the cause is found (the checker or a misreading of what it tracks), and if the checker, it lists such a test, test-first.

title: A terminal copy's box-drawn table pastes as broken lines
detail: Asked: "Also pasted tables look terrible" (08:03, the session summary pasted into a journal day). Why: the terminal draws a markdown table in box characters (┌ ├ └ │), each cell wrapped over several lines; the paste joins those lines as prose, so borders and cells run together. Done when: a box-drawn table in a terminal copy pastes as a markdown table, each cell's wrapped lines joined, its header row kept, test-first from a real copy, played in Helium.

title: Enter in a table adds a cell; no way out of a table without the markdown view
detail: Asked: "trying to enter out of a table just adds a new cell to that row, it doesn't exit the table. A way to exit the table without going into markdown mode would be good." (08:42) Why: a table pasted or typed at the end of an entry leaves nowhere to write after it except through ⌃⌘M. Done when: a key (chosen with the reader) leaves a table for a paragraph after it, test-first and played in Helium; the rest of what Enter does in a table unchanged.

title: A paused item's reactivation, read from a Helium run
detail: Asked: "yes, add P4" and "The details of S6.1 currently say it reactivates and it doesn't, so let's make it so." (11:3x, after the question whether S6.1 knows to reactivate). Why: S6.1's Reactivates when names a Helium failure, but nothing reads a run for it: a failure fails verify with no link to the item, and the reactivation rests on someone remembering. Done when: a paused item can name the text it waits for, and a Helium run whose output holds it starts the item, with the matching line as its note and the pages redrawn; S6.1 watches 'the bar did not show'; test-first.
